**USO, Monday 2026-11-23: the story and next-few-sessions catalysts**

**Bottom line:** USO's drop is a rational repricing of crude, not a fund-specific problem. The fall is a war-premium unwind on top of a coming supply glut. Oil lost a lot of risk premium this month, and the key swing factors are headline-driven in both directions.

**What happened today**
- WTI January settled at $80.17, down 4.5% (one source says 3.9%). That is its lowest close since August. Brent settled at $89.37, down about 3.5% and about 20% for the month. Brent topped $113 in late October, and London futures touched $118 the week before Nov 1. [Rigzone](https://www.rigzone.com/news/wire/oil_falls_as_trump_signals_iran_talks-23-nov-2026-185152-article/), [Nation Thailand](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/world/40073845)
- Trump gave diplomacy with Iran more time. He also said he might resume the war next year if talks fail. That pushes out the escalation timeline he had set before the midterms, so traders unwound the hedges they had put on against a weekend escalation.
- Libya restarted its Sharara pipeline, which adds supply.
- Tanker attacks in Hormuz, an Iranian attack on Bahrain and a reported Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia's Rabigh refinery did not stop the fall.
- SPY rose 4.7% the same day, so oil's fall is not a general selloff. It also fits a market that cares less about the war.

**The bearish story**
- The IEA sees a surplus of about 1.7 to 2 million barrels a day this quarter. Goldman flags a glut risk next year and sees Brent at $88 on average in 2027, falling to $78 by Dec 2027. JPMorgan sees WTI-area prices in the high $70s in the first half of 2027. [Nation Thailand, Nov 16](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/world/40073582)
- Hormuz shipments have recovered to about prewar levels, per [World Oil](https://worldoil.com/news/2026/11/1/opec-subgroup-keeps-oil-production-quotas-unchanged-for-december/).
- Chinese refinery throughput fell 8.1% from a year earlier in October.
- US commercial crude stocks rose 4.7M barrels (week to Nov 6) and 3.4M (week to Nov 13), to 417.8M. Stocks are still 3% below the five-year average. A preliminary Reuters poll expects another build of about 0.9M for the week to Nov 20.
- A tech and AI equity selloff has also hurt risk sentiment, per [Polyester Time](https://www.polyestertime.com/oil-prices-iran-war-brent-wti-outlook/).

**The bullish risks, which are real**
- BMI calls the export recovery "fragile". Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim tankers hit mines in the strait, but Reuters could not verify that. The US naval blockade of Iran continues, and Trump has warned that vessels testing it would be sunk.
- Bank of America notes that global stocks are low and that geopolitics still dominates price.
- A deal, a ceasefire breakdown or a new strike can reverse a week of selling in one session, as this month's range shows.
- Russian export disruptions from Ukrainian strikes and weather are also a risk.

**Catalysts in the next 1 to 10 sessions**
- **Tue-Wed:** The EIA weekly report is due Wednesday. A build confirms the glut story, and a draw could trigger a bounce.
- **Sun Nov 29:** The OPEC+ ministerial meeting sets 2027 policy. Rystad calls it "the much more important test". The capacity audit has been delayed, and the UAE wants a higher quota. The meeting falls on a weekend, so the reaction comes in the Nov 30 session. A decision to restore more output is bearish. A pause is probably already priced in.
- **Any day:** Iran talks, blockade incidents and Hormuz tanker attacks. As one analyst put it, "each weekend that passes without meaningful escalation leaves Monday vulnerable to selling pressure". That cuts both ways, because a weekend escalation would reverse it.
- **Macro:** The tech/AI equity swings.
- **Early December:** USO rolls into the next-month contract over five days starting at the beginning of the month, per [USCF](https://www.uscfinvestments.com/uso). The roll costs or earns more depending on the curve. I could not find a November 2026 curve snapshot. Backwardation was steep as of September, when the one-year implied WTI roll yield was about 21% ([Saxo](https://www.home.saxo/en-gb/content/articles/commodities/why-tight-commodity-markets-are-boosting-investor-returns-03092026)). If the curve has flattened with the glut, USO's roll yield has shrunk. Check the CME curve before sizing.

**Reading the tape against the story**
- The 19.8% fall over 20 sessions matches Brent's roughly 20% fall. USO is tracking crude closely.
- The after-hours quote of 133.57 and the overnight quote of 132.87 are roughly flat, so there is no immediate overnight rebound or breakdown.
- USO sits just above its 200-day average (129.47). A break below it would add technical selling.
- The stock is stretched and oversold: RSI 34, 2.9 ranges below its 20-day average. That raises the odds of a bounce, but the fall is news-driven with a bearish forecast backing it, so oversold alone is a weak reason to buy.
- Volume was light at 0.9x normal, so the move was not capitulation.

- I found no current USO NAV, premium or discount, or November curve data. The fund's page fields were blank.
- My search for the Nov 23 OPEC+ expectations found only coverage up to early November.

**Costco (COST): the drop looks mechanical, not news. $30 special dividend, ex-date most likely Nov 24.**

**The screen's signal is probably the dividend**
- Costco declared a $30 per share special dividend on Nov 10. It is worth about $13.3B, the record date is Nov 24 and it is payable Dec 4.
- Costco never named an ex-dividend date. By Nasdaq rule, a dividend under 25% of the share price goes ex on the record date. $30 is about 2.8% of the price, so ex-date is most likely Tuesday Nov 24.
- The 7:30 PM CT overnight session is already trading Tuesday's date, so it should be ex-dividend. The 6:45 PM CT after-hours print of 1,104.99 was still cum-dividend, which fits that.
- Adjusting for the dividend, the reference price is about 1,067.91 (1,097.91 minus 30). The overnight 1,071.50 is then about +0.3%, not -2.4%.
- Confirm the ex-date with the broker or Nasdaq before sizing anything. The company's announcement and SEC filing don't state it.
- I found no news explaining a real selloff. A search for tonight's move turned up nothing for Nov 24.

**The story**
- **Sales are strong.** FY2026 sales were $297.2B, up 10.1%. Q4 sales were $93.9B, up 11.2%, with EPS of $6.75 against a $6.54 consensus. That EPS included a one-time $0.15 tariff-refund benefit.
- **Digital and footprint.** Digitally enabled comps were up 19.5%. Costco has 939 warehouses and plans 33 openings in FY2027.
- **October sales (released Nov 4).** Sales were $24.50B, up 12.6%. Total comps were up 11.1%, but only 7.3% excluding gas and currency. Digital was up 22.5%. Part of the headline is gasoline.
- **Cash and buyback.** Cash was $20.2B at fiscal year-end. The special dividend uses about two-thirds of it. A new $4B buyback runs to Nov 2030.
- **Analysts.** JPMorgan target $1,150, Bernstein $1,155, Mizuho $1,100 (it also dropped Costco from its Top Picks). Tigress $1,250. The average target was about $1,092 on Nov 13.
- **Valuation.** Forward P/E is about 46 to 48. Zacks rates it Hold. One commentator reads the large special dividend and the small buyback use (about $847M in FY2026) as management seeing the stock as fully priced.

**What could move it over the next 1 to 10 sessions**
- **Ex-dividend reset (Nov 24).** The roughly $30 gap should not count as a signal or as a short setup.
- **Dividend capture unwinding.** Holders who bought for the payout may sell after the ex-date. The stock was up 9.4% over 20 sessions into the date. I found no evidence on how much of that was dividend-driven.
- **November sales, early December.** Costco usually reports in early December. The comparison is Nov 2025, when sales rose 8.1% and comps 6.9%. Another 7%-plus comp excluding gas supports the stock. A slowdown has hit it before, as with the July 2026 report, when shares dropped about 1.2% after hours.
- **Q1 FY2027 earnings, Dec 10 after the close.** That is probably beyond a 1 to 10 session hold, depending on entry. Consensus is about $4.87 to $4.90 EPS on $74.3B revenue. The stock has often slipped after hours on past beats.
